lines.en: I find myself alongside my slightly wonderful (but mostly annoying) kouhai on the way back from another uneventful day at school.
Or at least what was an uneventful day up until the very end of it, when I was somehow suckered into assisting Imani and some of the other girls in cleaning the pool.
But that isn’t what I’ve decided to share with you today.
What I have decided to share is the tail end of a long walk to the bar after a hard day’s work because it’s moments like these where my mind begins to wander.
And as it detaches itself from the inside of my skull and saunters off down alleys unexplored, I must summon the me who once was to take over in its stead.
But that “me” overcomplicates things.
It turns otherwise pleasant moments upside down when it remembers that it and we are undeserving of quiet moments like this.
We’re undeserving of long walks to the bar or bubble tea or the pruning of our hands after soaking them in soap and water for hours on end.
But no one cares what we do or don’t deserve. No one cares if things are complicated or not.
All that we want is to watch one thing transform into something else. That’s what keeps life fresh. That’s what keeps our interactions notable.
So I will disguise myself as a passable human being and communicate with this girl in a way that is mostly normal, but fractionally strange based on an unwanted substitute...
It’ll be fine, though.
Everything will be fine.
She’ll laugh and smile and flirt and laugh again because that is what she does as a slightly wonderful (but mostly annoying) kouhai. Which is, again, fine.
But it’s not what anyone wants to see.
What we want is the closing of a gap between two people who would be better off remaining three feet apart in perpetuity, because that closure breaks the silence.
It interrupts our walk.
And it lays down the foundation of the real story here. Not just the one we got conned into watching after pressing the wrong button on a metaphorical TV remote.
Why can I not just walk home in peace?
Why does everything have to be an event?
: Senpai. Tell me a joke.
: Knock knock.
: Who’s there?
: No.
: No who?
: That was it, wasn’t it?
: Funny, right?
: No! And why did you make me knock if you were just going to turn me away?
: Because your disappointment is funny to me and comedy is subjective. It’s not my fault if you don’t laugh.
: Mm.
: Knock knock.
: I’m not falling for it again, Senpai. We can just go back to talking about boring normal stuff since that’s apparently all you’re capable of.
: Well, it’s not as if we can make idle chit-chat about how our day was when we spent the entire thing together.

: Correct me if I’m wrong here, but I’m pretty sure that falls into “boring normal stuff.” Tell me something interesting. As my elder, isn’t it your job to keep me entertained on long walks like this?
: Uhh...no? As the younger, more energetic teacher here, shouldn’t you be the one keeping things “entertaining” while I just...nod and say something mildly sexual every once in a while?

: Maybe. But you haven’t even done that. And if you bring that attitude to the bar, the rest of the girls are going to wind up kicking you out of the friend group no matter how hard I try to stop them.
: I think I’ll be okay. Despite what little time we’ve all shared together, I think we’re a pretty tight-knit group by now. Besides, my role as the token male would be hard to just outright replace.
: Ooh! Then that means my role as the token “young one” will be hard to outright replace too! Hooray for us! We’re both-
: Wait. You thought I was going to say something else just now, didn’t you?
: I literally didn’t even move my mouth.
: Likely story! Now, either tell me a joke or I’m quitting Kumon-mi High and getting a job in the sinkhole.
: It was nice working with you, Imani. Sorry we never got to make out.
: Don’t be. You’re not missing much if Rika’s scale is anywhere near the same as yours.
: I’m not sure if it’s rude to say this or not, but I’m pretty sure her scale is a lot...larger than mine.
: It would have been a little less rude without the awkward pause and emphasis placed on larger. But yeah...you’re probably not wrong.
: Just don’t repeat that to her, okay? She’s a little sensitive when it comes to people pointing out her past and...you’re looking away from me.
: You already did that, didn’t you?
: Not...purposely.
: Hah...what am I going to do with you?
: As if taking over in school isn’t already enough, it’s like you want me to take over in-
: Wait, hold that thought. That’s probably one of the girls right now.
: How can I hold your thought? That’s not how that works.
: Hello?...
: Oh, hey! I was actually just talking about you...
: No...It wasn’t about how much you like pizza. And I’m not sure why you would have assumed that, but...what’s up?
: Wait, really?...
: Like...not at all?
As Imani converses with who I can only imagine is Rika, my phone begins to ring as well...
: Hello?
: Arakawa — I need you to listen carefully.
: You are being set up.
: ...What?

: I am a good friend who has not revealed any of the things you said to me the other night about your childhood friend or your feelings concerning Imani, so I want you to know this has nothing to do with me.
: And also that I am sorry. I tried.
: I’m not really sure what-
: No one else is coming to the bar. It is a calculated effort coordinated by Osako and Rika to get you and Imani alone together. I had no part in this.
: ...Uh-huh.
: Ah. So that’s what’s going on.
: It won’t be a problem, will it? The two of you being alone together.
: Not at all. But thanks for letting me know you had nothing to do with it, I guess.
: Of course.
: Just also know that I am not opposed to the idea of you having sex with her. In fact, if it were not for your “feelings,” I would say that would be the best outcome possible.
: I’ll keep that in mind, Wakana. Goodnight.
: Wait, Arakawa — there’s one more thing.
: There always is. What is it this time?
: Nothing important. Just that-
: I want to fucking die.
Both of us hang up the phone and...I accept that tonight’s “silence” is going to be broken in even more ways than I initially expected.
: So, uhh...looks like it’s just gonna be you and me tonight.
: Still down?
: We’ve been alone a million times before. Why should this be any different?
: Exactly! This is just another night. Just two friends going out to the bar for drinks. Nothing weird about it unless we make it weird, right?
: You’re starting to get close to making it weird, Imani.
: No. You’re making things weird by saying that I’m starting to make things weird. Come on, Senpai. You should know better than that.
: How about just...neither one of us talks until we have a drink in our hand. Cool?
: Deal.
I take up Imani’s offer to remain quiet until we’re equipped with vials of liquid courage and revel in the return of a hastily departed silence.
It doesn’t last long, however, as we know these roads like the backs of our hands and have navigated to this exact bar time and time again.
Just never without anyone else.
And confronting that will be fine for me-
But will it be fine for Imani?
Will she be able to overlook her innate desire to fuck me in the same way that I have taught myself how to bypass those urges and feelings in regard to her?
Judging by her current demeanor, I’d say the answer is yes. I’d say that she can do that.
But I may very well just be giving her the benefit of the doubt because she’s smarter and older than the majority of girls I deal with on a daily basis.
It’s easy to look at people like them and predict their next moves because the majority of them are just as predictable as girls that age are meant to be.
But I still don’t know much about Imani.
I don’t know anything about the way she thinks because I’ve yet to learn what she thinks at all.
And all signs point to this being a good opportunity to learn, but...
: Senpai...
But I feel like we’re just going to wind up talking about me again.
: What’s up?
: This isn’t so bad...is it? Just you and me here, I mean.
: Did you expect it to be bad?
: No! It’s just, like...this is different. You know? We see each other all the time, but...the context of how we’re seeing each other makes things kind of...different. Ish.
: I feel the same as always, pretty much.
: Is that because...you’ve already got someone who kind of...twists your world into a giant knot?
: A little clarification would probably be nice right now. I'm not sure how to interpret that.
: I just mean, like...
: Well, look at it this way. A lot of the time, when people talk about knots, it’s with some kind of...negative connotation.
: Like...oh. My stomach is “in knots.” Or...I feel all “knotted up” inside. But what about all of the times where knots are good?
: Imani, how drunk are you right now?
: I am zero drunk, Senpai. We just got here. But, like...think about shoelaces. Or...shibari or something like that. There are a ton of situations where knots are a good thing.
: They’re something that provides safety or security and...keeps shit in place.
: And, you know...frankly...
: I can’t think of anything more “secure” than dating an idol.
Here we go...
: Niki Nakayama...impressive.
: And here I thought you were going to marry her sister one day.
: Her sister is a teenage girl. Did you actually think I was planning on marrying her?
: No. I’m just not great at talking about heavy subjects and wind up using sarcasm as a backbone sometimes. Please forgive me, Senpai. I’m still learning.
: Well, at least we’ve got that in common.
: We’ve got a lot in common. Just I’m the one who winds up having to do all of the heavy lifting since I’m the extrovert here.
: The reality is though, Senpai...deep down, I don’t really want to be.
: It’d be nice just relaxing and not having to worry about how everyone looks at me or...what everyone is thinking all the time, but I haven’t really figured out how to make that happen just yet.
: So instead, I keep things moving. Keep my expectations in line with the direction things are already flowing in and...just kind of...give things a push when they need to be pushed.
: Is this you telling me I need a “push?”
: Not at all. I like you the way you are. I don’t think people have to be perfect or...even good for that matter.
: Like, don’t get me wrong- I’d be much quicker to tie myself to someone who doesn’t go around ruining everyone’s lives than someone who does-
: But I also think that reducing people to something as simplistic as the...history of their decisions concerning all things “morality” doesn’t paint the full picture.
: So...that wasn’t even remotely close to you telling me I need a push. You’re either just demonstrably bad at explaining things or I’m demonstrably bad at getting the point.
: It’s probably me. What I’m really saying is that if I vibe with somebody, I’m more inclined to overlook any disagreements we have concerning moral alignments or...anything like that.
: Sure, but...what does that have to do with Niki exactly? How did we get from her to this?
: I don’t know.
: I’ve got no fucking clue what I’m doing, Senpai.

: It’s not even like I’m running in circles either. It’s like I’m lost somewhere in the middle of the track and I can’t even figure out how to get back onto it or...what direction I’m supposed to be running in.
: But everyone seems to think it’ll just...click or something. Or they don’t realize I’m lost and assume I’m just pretending to be because it’ll make everyone laugh when...
: When the truth is...I want someone to take my hand and show me where to go or...or get lost with me.
: I just haven’t figured out how to stop...reflexively pulling away any time someone tries to reach out just yet.
: If any of that sounded weird, you can just assume I’m already drunk.
: All of it sounded a little weird, but I’m not going to do that. Especially since you haven't taken a single sip of your drink since you last told me you weren't drunk.
: Instead, I’m just going to ask if you’re okay.
: I think so. I’ve probably just thrown myself into rant-mode because we don’t ever really do things like this alone and I’m excited to finally get to...connect with you.
: I’m just not sure if we’re really...connecting the way I want. You know?...
: This...uh...
: Niki Nakayama...are you guys, like...
: What’s the deal?

Imani begins to play with the tab on her beer can, flicking it and bending it to compensate for the lack of sound inside the bar or to just...soothe some sort of mental craving she’s having right now.
I can’t say for sure as, again, I have no clue what her deal is. But, of course, we’re talking about me again.
We’re talking about me because that’s all that ever happens and...and 99%% of the time, it’s all I want.
But despite these tinted glasses that I’ve been peering through in order to see her, I want to know why she spends so much time agonizing over me when there is no reason to at all.
She doesn’t have to worry about Niki — she should worry about herself. About her dreams of helping children or the time she could spend on someone who doesn’t mind sacrificing a friendship.
: The deal is that I love her.
Her motions with the tab become more rapid...anxious. And I can sense that it’s only a few hard pulls from being snapped clean off of the aluminum.
: Do you want to hear more? Or does that suffice?
: Is she good to you? She seemed a little...bossy.
: She is. On both counts. Her bossiness is just a side effect of her archetype. In all actuality, she’s a very good person. And she cares about me more than I deserve.
: That’s not the answer you wanted to hear, was it?
: I’m just happy you’re happy, Senpai. It sounds like you two are a good match.
: I’m probably just not really understanding her yet. Maybe in time. I don’t know.
: Do you want to understand her? Because she might be open to coming to the bar sometime, you know. I could always invite her.
: Yeah, I...don’t really want to get to know her.
: Idols aren’t really my thing.
: I’m glad you’re happy, though. Seriously. You deserve it.
: Do I really, though?
: Yes...of course you do. Even if you’re corrupting the denizens of our poor classroom every single day, you’re still a human being. And we all deserve to feel loved in one way or another.
: Do you have anyone like that, Imani? Someone who makes you feel loved? And no, I’m not just speaking romantically. I mean in general.
: Come on, Senpai. Do you really think I’d be acting like this if I did?
: I haven’t had anyone like that in...years. And even then, I'm pretty sure I only believed I was loved and that...I’ve never really felt it the way you have.
: I’m sorry for prying and...making you talk about stuff like your love life when we’re not really supposed to be doing that, but-
: Do you really think I care about what we’re “supposed to be doing?”
: I told you because I wanted to tell you. I wanted to share a piece of myself with you because I want you to do the same for me. That’s what friends do. Probably.
: Honestly, I don’t have very many- so I can’t confirm that.
: You and me both, Senpai.
: That’s just one more reason I...like being with you so much.
: Are you...going to say anything else?
: I was waiting to see what you’d do next.
: But I think I get it now.
: And I think I need another drink.
The tab on her beer can finally breaks off.
And just as it does, the silence returns.
And the knots in my stomach protect me from nothing.
Imani’s affection has increased to [imani_love]!
